adjudicated_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients at (g,n)=(6,6). Let X denote the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6} of dimension 21, and let T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified by FND-0001 with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21). Let Y be any closed substack of X, write U:=X minus Y, and let T_Z:=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(U;Q)(21)) be the associated kernel-form term (the ATT-0120/FND-0180 interface when Y is the reduced classifying-image closure). Poincare-Verdier duality on the smooth ambient identifies cohomology with supports along Y with Borel-Moore homology of Y: topologically H^{BM}_k(Y) isomorphic to H^{2d-k}(X,U) for the closed embedding of Y into the oriented real 2d-manifold underlying X (Iversen IX.4.7), and algebraically H^{26}_Y(X;Q) isomorphic to H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)(21). This identification requires no closed regular embedding of Y, no lci or purity-of-codimension hypothesis, no Gysin map, and no degree shift by twice a codimension. FND-0180 already records that the same duality intertwines ordinary open restriction with Borel-Moore corestriction, so T_Z equals the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)->T in the sense of FND-0168(3a). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, hence W_{-16} is exact on the Borel-Moore localization sequence, and T_Z is a quotient of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q). Duality convention as in FND-0165: H^{BM}_k(-;Q):=Hom(H_c^k(-;Q),Q) with no extra Tate twist. Deligne's weight bound, recorded for Borel-Moore homology by Hanamura-Saito, gives that H_c^k has weights at most k and therefore H^{BM}_k has weights at least -k, so the bottom step W_{-k}H^{BM}_k is pure of weight -k. Over C this piece is polarizable (graded-polarizable Deligne mixed Hodge structures, including the simplicial-scheme formalism of Hodge III 8.3 applied to an etale atlas of the finite-type stack Y). Thus W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16. Polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of a fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category (FND-0033), so a quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is a finite direct sum of Q(8). Hence, for any such Y and in particular for the ATT-0120 support, the condition that W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8) is sufficient for T_Z to be a finite direct sum of Q(8), which is the C66-TATE-SUPPORT conclusion. The condition is sufficient, not necessary: non-Tate summands of the source may die in the map to T. The statement does not assert that the source is Tate, does not prove T_Z Tate, and says nothing about support-exhaustion T_Z=T. Stack-level compactly supported cohomology of Y is used only through the Poincare-Verdier mixed Hodge structure already granted by FND-0180 on the smooth pair (X,U); this does not reopen the FND-0165 exclusion of an independent stack-level H_c formalism. FND-0052 and FND-0168(5a)/(5b) remain binding for any Gysin-style computation that would identify the supports group with a codimension shift of ordinary cohomology of Y, but they are not required for this sufficiency.
contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the corrected statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0001 (purity for smooth proper stacks) and with RED-0001 (the named T_Z is a subobject of the open input). Contested passage in ATT-0121 section 6: the attempt correctly records that a Gysin identification of H^{26}_Y(M_{6,6}) with a degree-shifted cohomology of Y needs a closed regular embedding or stratified lci structure, which FND-0052 and FND-0168(5a)/(5b) leave undischarged, and that no map H_c^{16}(Z)->T is supplied. The illicit 'thus' is the claim that those missing Gysin data are necessary to constrain Hodge types of the named kernel T_Z. REV-0171's strongest attack and the candidate key kernel-form-tate-reduces-to-lowest-weight-bm-of-the-support correctly reject that necessity. FND-0168(3) already gives the exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)->T->W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q), and FND-0180 already identifies T_Z with the image of the first map via Poincare-Verdier on the smooth ambient, with no regular immersion. The new content is purity of that source group and the resulting sufficiency for C66-TATE-SUPPORT. Duality is Hom(H_c^k,Q) with no extra Tate twist, matching FND-0165 and Hanamura-Saito (H^{BM}_j is the dual of H_c^j; weights of H^{BM}_j are at least -j). Wikipedia/Iversen IX.4.7 supplies H^{BM}_i(Y)=H^{m-i}(X,X minus Y) for any closed embedding of a locally compact space into an oriented manifold, so the identification needs no Gysin, lci, or pure-codimension hypothesis. Deligne Hodge III section 8.3 equips simplicial schemes with mixed Hodge structures, which covers finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks via etale atlases and therefore does not reopen FND-0165's exclusion of an independent stack-level compact-support formalism: the MHS on W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y) is the one already used by FND-0180. FND-0180's closing remark that FND-0052 and FND-0168(5) remain binding wherever T_Z must be computed or shown Tate is a method remark about Gysin-style shifts, not a theorem that Gysin is required for sufficiency; the two findings are compatible once that sentence is read as not claiming necessity. Distinct from FND-0033, which records semisimplicity for subquotients of T rather than for the support's own lowest-weight Borel-Moore group. Distinct from FND-0168(3a), which records necessity of T_Z-Tate for T-Tate along a subobject, not sufficiency of source-Tate for T_Z-Tate along a quotient. Not a merge into FND-0180: that finding names the kernel-form interface and does not record purity of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y) or the sufficiency statement. Candidate wording corrections applied below: replace 'any finite-type object' by the FND-0165 duality convention plus the FND-0180 Poincare-Verdier MHS on a closed substack of the smooth ambient; replace 'with polarizable graded piece' by the statement that W_{-k}H^{BM}_k is itself pure polarizable of weight -k; record that FND-0180 supplies the image identification, while Deligne/Hanamura-Saito supply the weight bound; and keep the condition sufficient, not necessary, and silent on T_Z=T.

scope.mathematical_scope: Gysin-free sufficiency: Tate type of the lowest-weight Borel-Moore group of a closed support implies Tate type of the associated kernel-form term T_Z. Does not prove that source group is Tate, does not assert support-exhaustion T_Z=T, and does not identify supports cohomology with a codimension shift of ordinary cohomology of Y.

closed regular embedding, lci, or Gysin for Y
a map from the cohomology of Z to T
